title: A changing cultural landscape
lead: A city of cultural institutions, under pressure from the pandemic and changing economic conditions.
caption: Historical scope · closure verification still required
method: First establish what existed, what closed, and what remains uncertain. A missing grant or directory record is not proof of closure.
legend:
Dark centers: current directory records
Fine rings: visual emphasis, not closure status
source:
Map: DCLA directory, Oct 2026; NYC DCP NTA geography.
Historical operating status is not yet verified.
next: NEXT / Establish the FY2024 funding baseline.

title: The FY2024 baseline
lead: Start with the observed funding record. Count recipients separately from physical venues.
caption: $15.42M recorded in FY2024
method: Signed transactions are summed by recipient and fiscal year. Column height shows positive net funding. Unlocated recipients remain in the overall totals.
source:
NEA / USAspending processed transaction records.
434 recipients with positive annual net funding; totals include signed amounts.
next: NEXT / Hold the geography steady and compare FY2025.

title: A sharp annual funding gap
lead: Funding fell between fiscal years. The map shows a change in recorded awards, not a map of confirmed closures.
caption: $15.42M → $6.47M · approximately $8.95M less
method: Watch each column move to its FY2025 value. Addresses and height scale stay fixed. A ground-level mark remains when positive funding reaches zero; this does not establish closure.
legend:
Rose: lower FY2025 funding · sage: increase
Hollow marker: no positive FY2025 funding
source:
Same processed NEA transaction scope as Chapter 02.
177 recipients have positive FY2025 net funding; 358 have lower net amounts.
next: NEXT / See how institutions fall within neighborhoods.

title: Institutions become neighborhoods
lead: NTAs are Neighborhood Tabulation Areas: a consistent geography for comparing local conditions.
caption: Color identifies NTA; height still shows FY2025 recipient funding
method: Group recipient addresses by NTA. Each neighborhood gets its own hue, carried into the next chapter. Colors identify groups, not funding rank or poverty.
legend:
Translucent patches: NTA groupings
Matching colors link recipients and neighborhoods
source:
NYC DCP 2020 NTA geography + processed recipient addresses.
Colors distinguish neighboring groups; they are not a ranking.

title: Where are losses concentrated?
lead: Neighborhood totals reveal patterns that individual award records can hide.
caption: Same NTA hue · pale FY2024 / saturated FY2025
method: Pair annual neighborhood totals using a common neighborhood height scale. This scale differs from the recipient views. Negative net amounts appear as outlined ground marks; click to read signed values.
legend:
Rose: lower NTA net funding · sage: higher
Stronger tint: larger absolute dollar change
source:
Processed NEA_NTA_observed_2024_2025_cents table.
Final named comparisons and ranked labels to be audited.
next: NEXT / Ask what surrounds the observed losses.

title: Funding loss meets local conditions
lead: Does reduced funding overlap with high poverty and fewer nearby cultural organizations?
caption: 12 mapped recipients selected by largest dollar decline, one per coordinate
method: Count directory records within a projected half-mile (2,640 US survey feet) of these 12 examples. Co-located and duplicate directory records remain included. Poverty and visitor-origin comparisons are still pending.
legend:
Translucent rings: half-mile proximity
Centers: selected recipients with reduced funding
source:
Actual recipient coordinates + DCLA directory locations.
Poverty, audience origins, and measured visitor journeys are not shown.
next: NEXT / Check which disciplines the directory represents.

title: Which cultural practices are present?
lead: Separate theater, music, dance, and visual arts before asking which disciplines experienced larger losses.
caption: Directory categories shown; NEA linkage still pending
method: Use recorded discipline fields first. Link recipient identifiers or reviewed name matches to funding records. Keep unknown categories visible; do not infer targeting from location alone.
legend:
Rose: theater · sage: music
Yellow: dance · lavender: visual arts
source:
DCLA Cultural Organizations directory, October 2026. Colors distinguish all 21 recorded or unknown discipline categories.
These categories have not yet been linked to NEA funding declines.
next: NEXT / Move explicitly from observation to a proposal.

title: An alliance for collective resilience
lead: Could shared reserves and nearby partnerships cushion a future funding shock?
caption: A design scenario, not an observed financial network
method: Test an adjustable annual savings rate, contribution rule, and support floor. Compare outcomes with the observed baseline. A $25,000 floor is a test assumption, not a proven survival budget.
legend:
Dashed connections: proposed relationships
Layered rings: hypothetical shared support
source:
Scenario direction informed by SMT_Sandbox.
Connections are illustrative; no transfers or survival outcomes are asserted.
next: END / Compare assumptions, geography, and distributional outcomes.
